p: The book of the vision of: The vision or revelation, which God commanded Nahum to write concerning the Ninevites.
Elkoshite: That is, born in a poor village in the tribe of Simeon.
is furious: With his own he is but angry for a time, but his anger is never appeased toward the reprobate, even though he defers it for a time.
LORD is slow to anger: Thus the wicked would make God's mercy an occasion to sin, but the Prophet wishes them to consider his power and justice.

Who can stand before his indignation: If all creatures are at God's commandment, and none are able to resist his wrath, will man flatter himself, and think by any means to escape, when he provokes his God to anger?
a strong hold in the day: Lest the faithful should be discouraged by hearing the power of God, he shows them that his mercy appertains to them, and that he has care over them.
place thereof: Signifying that God will suddenly destroy Nineveh and the Assyrians in such a way, that they will lie in perpetual darkness, and never recover their strength again.

imagine against the LORD: He shows that the undertakings of the Assyrians against Judah and the Church were against God, and therefore he would so destroy them the first time, that he would not need to return the second time.

thorns: Though the Assyrians think themselves like thorns that prick on all sides, yet the Lord will set fire on them, and as drunken men are not able to stand against any force, so they will not be able to resist him at all.
come out of thee: Which may be understood either of Sennacherib, or of the whole body of the people of Nineveh.

quiet: Though they think themselves in most safety, and of greatest strength, yet when God will pass by, he will destroy them: nonetheless, he comforts his Church, and promises to stop punishing them by the Assyrians.
sown: Meaning, Sennacherib, who would have no more children, but be slain in the house of his gods; 2Ki 19:36-37.
peace: Which peace the Jews would enjoy by the death of Sennacherib.
